subject: Recap: Open-model offramp discovery + success criteria (Cloudocity)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Suarez <elena@cloudocity.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Open-model offramp discovery + success criteria (Cloudocity)

Hi Elena / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard on the call and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. I’ve kept this focused on the migration/compatibility items we discussed.

Pain points you described
- Monthly spend: ~USD 120k/mo across OpenAI (primary) + Anthropic (safety/rerank). Cost is the top driver for evaluating an off‑ramp.
- Latency variability at peak (p95 spikes during batch ingest / live product traffic).
- Feature gaps between your current APIs (streaming + function-calling + embeddings) and some open-model runtimes.
- Safety pipeline: you run Anthropic models for content safety and a downstream reranker today.

Current stack notes (as called out on the call)
- Production: OpenAI completions/streaming with function-calling for structured actions.
- Anthropic used for a safety + reranking lane.
- Embeddings stored in Pinecone (approx 25M vectors).
- Fine-tune vs instruction-tune: you prefer instruction-tuning + adapters rather than full fine-tune for faster turnaround.

Success criteria for a PoC / pilot (draft)
- API parity: function-calling + streaming + embeddings available without major client changes.
- Fidelity: <5% regression on our canonical prompt set (we’ll jointly agree on prompts).
- Cost: target ~40% reduction in per-token spend versus current blended rate (ballpark).
- Latency: p95 for short completions (<= 450ms) and stable under expected concurrency.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS or equivalent for key material.

Model shortlist to evaluate (we’ll adapt after your sample prompts)
- Llama 2 (70B, quantized variants) — strong foundation for instruction tuning.
- Mistral Instruct 30B — competitive for throughput/cost tradeoffs.
- Redwood-Raven-13B (optimized 8-bit path) — candidate for low-latency, cost-sensitive endpoints.

Suggested next steps
1) You share 3 representative prompt profiles + weekly token/traffic profile (samples by Mon Nov 30).
2) Redwood to produce a short evaluation plan and estimated cost matrix for the three model candidates (deliverable: evaluation plan + rough TCO).
3) Technical deep dive (Redwood infra + compatibility checklist) — propose Wed Dec 2 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET.
4) PoC SOW draft (6-week pilot, scope: canonical prompts, metrics, model variants) — attached draft.

Attached: cloudocity_poc_scope_20261127.xlsx, redwood-offramp-checklist.pdf

If this summary misses anything important, please call it out and I’ll update. Happy to tighten the success criteria with you.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0217

From: Elena Suarez <elena@cloudocity.com>

Cc: Mark Bowers <mark@cloudocity.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T14:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Open-model offramp discovery + success criteria (Cloudocity)

Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. This matches our internal notes closely. A few clarifications from our side:

- Stack detail: production is currently on GPT-4.1 via OpenAI with streaming responses and function-calling to populate our action items. Anthropic is used in a parallel safety lane — we do not pipe Anthropic into the product path directly, it’s used for classification/reranking.
- Embeddings: Pinecone holds ~25M vectors; reindexing is a concern for us — we want embedding parity and identical dims/encoding if possible.
- Data residency: we need all inference for EU customers to run in eu-west-1. That’s a hard constraint for the pilot subset.
- Cost target: 40% reduction is attractive but we’re also sensitive to engineering lift for changes in function-calling semantics.

We can share sample prompts and traffic by Monday. Also looping in Legal for SOW review (cc’d cloudocity-legal).

Elena
VP Product, Cloudocity
elena@cloudocity.com

Thanks Elena / Ben — quick technical clarifications from my side before the deep dive: 

- SOC2 / compliance: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and support customer-managed KMS; for EU residency we support region pinning for inference in our Private and Dedicated products.
- Function-calling parity: we have a compatibility layer that maps common function-calling patterns (name/arguments/call_id) — we’ll prepare a short compatibility matrix for OpenAI and Anthropic patterns.
- Embeddings: we’ll run a small compatibility job against your sample vectors to validate distance metrics prior to any reindex.
- Ballpark token cost estimates: we’ll include a ballpark TCO for each model candidate in the evaluation plan; to make that tight we’ll need the sample prompt traffic and average token lengths.

I can lead the technical deep dive next Wed; propose 60–75 minutes to cover API mappings, security, and a short walk-through of our evaluation harness. Confirm if Wed Dec 2 10:00 PT works.

—Neha
